source_text: Quibus duobus si creditis, id est Dei nec opera mala esse, nec iniqua iudicia; totum traducis dogma conteritur: sicut e regione, traducis impietate suscepta, haec duo, conditio Dei atque iudicatio, per quae solum Deus potest intellegi, destruuntur.
pass_a_gloss: If you believe these two things, that is, that God's works are not evil, nor his judgments unjust, the whole dogma of the tradux is crushed: just as from the opposite side, the impiety of the tradux having been taken up, these two, God's creating and his judging, through which alone God can be understood, are destroyed.

lemmas.lexica: LS tradux=vine-shoot/layer; Blaise tradux peccati=transmission of sin by descent
LS malum; Blaise malum naturale vs malum voluntatis
LS opus; Blaise God's works vs devil's

pass_b_english: If you believe these two things, that God’s works are not evil and his judgments are not unjust, the whole doctrine of inherited sin is crushed. Conversely, if the impiety of inherited sin is accepted, these two things, God’s creation and his judgment, through which alone God can be understood, are destroyed.

choices.why: Julian's polemic target is inherited sin as a natural evil (malum naturale), the vine-layer metaphor, not a later systematic 'original sin' slogan and not soul-traducianism as such.
rejected: original sin (later system as default gloss)
traducianism of the soul (not the load here)

choices.why: Julian's Manichaean charge: an evil that is a nature, not a will's act.
Julian's charge against Augustine: treating evil as a nature rather than as will.

anf_compare.notes: Victorian English of some of Julian survives inside NPNF Augustine (chiefly On Marriage and Concupiscence and related anti-Pelagian books). NPNF was not copied. Pass A is a literal gloss of Augustinus.it Latin of Julian's words only; Augustine's replies in the same locus are excluded.

speaker: Julian of Eclanum (words preserved in Augustine, Opus imperfectum contra Iulianum); Augustine's reply at this locus is excluded.
